turns.text: Student A, what makes an observation different from an interpretation?
An observation records what happened. Saying a quiet student did not understand adds an interpretation we have not checked.
Student B, how could we check that interpretation?
Ask for a written explanation too. I would compare that with the discussion before deciding. That builds on A's distinction.

criteria.title: Reasoning with evidence
criteria.description: Explain claims and connect them to observable evidence. Record insufficient evidence separately from a low score.

criteria.title: Constructive engagement
criteria.description: Respond to or develop another contribution. Silence alone does not establish understanding or its absence.

passages.text: An observation describes an event. An interpretation proposes what that event means. A claim about understanding requires more evidence than the absence of speech.

documents.title: Fictional notes: checking a claim
documents.source: Fictional course handout B (authored for development)

passages.text: Check a proposed explanation against another source of evidence. A short written response can complement a discussion, but differences should be investigated rather than assumed to indicate weakness.
